title: Cofinality of compatible raw coefficient refinements
statement:
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme with a selected finite affine gluing presentation $\mathsf G_S$, main chart rings $A_a$, and the finite principal-open piece maps $\rho_p:A_b\to(A_a)_{f_p}$ that are restrictions of its genuine overlap identifications, as in [def-nagata-affine-raw-refinement-system]. Let $C$ be any raw coefficient tuple in that definition; in the approximation construction it is the tuple at $\lambda_{\mathrm{coeff}}(S)$ whose existence and agreement with the original restrictions are asserted by [lemma-nagata-affine-gluing-coefficients-descend].
The explicitly defined preorder $I(C)$ of [def-nagata-affine-raw-refinement-system] is nonempty and directed. More precisely it contains $C$, and if $B,B'\in I(C)$, the tuple of subrings generated by $B_a\cup B'_a$ is an object above both. For any finite subsets $T_a\subseteq A_a$ on the finitely many main charts and any $B\in I(C)$, there is $B'\in I(C)$ with $B\leq B'$ and $T_a\subseteq B'_a$ for all $a$. Consequently the inclusion cocone of the chart diagram $B\mapsto B_a$ has colimit $A_a$ in commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], for every $a$. The cocone maps and all piece-map comparisons are the actual subring inclusions and localized maps in the definition; in particular they identify the limiting restricted maps with the original $\rho_p$.
This is an extension/cofinality statement about raw coefficient tuples. It does not assert any finite-stage open-preservation, identity, inverse, or cocycle condition and does not select equation witnesses or a common valid stage. The requirement that the partial maps come from the overlap identifications of one scheme is essential: this is not a cofinality assertion for subrings stable under arbitrary finitely many ring endomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 07RN (lemma-approximate), proof: finite affine induction and compatible coefficient refinement preorder; supporting raw-subring cofinality formulation for blueprint order 336 (agent statement, not a verbatim assertion of 07RN)

proof.text: By [def-nagata-affine-raw-refinement-system], the tuple C itself satisfies the defining conditions for I(C). For B,B' in I(C), choose finite ring-generating sets E_a for B_a and E'_a for B'_a, and put H_a=Z[E_a union E'_a] inside A_a. These are finitely generated subrings containing C_a, B_a and B'_a. For p:a to b, every element of H_b is an integral polynomial in E_b union E'_b. Its image under rho_p is the same polynomial in the images of these generators. Those images lie in (B_a)_{f_p} or (B'_a)_{f_p}, hence in (H_a)_{f_p}. Thus H is an object of I(C) above both B and B'. Here the localized inclusions send x/f_p^n to the identical fraction; they are injective: if such a fraction becomes zero in (A_a)_{f_p}, some power of f_p annihilates x in A_a, and the same equality holds in the subring. This also justifies all localizations viewed as subrings in the definition.

source.place: Tag 07RN (lemma-approximate), compatible coefficient refinement preorder; elementary subring and fraction verification for the raw variant

proof.text: Fix finite T_a and B in I(C). Choose finite ring-generating sets E_a of B_a, and let L_a=T_a union E_a. Form another selected finite affine gluing presentation of the same S, keeping all main charts, all original overlap pieces, and all their original maps. In the self-overlap U_a intersection U_a=U_a append U_a itself to the finite affine overlap cover. Give this added member the finite basic-open cover consisting of D(1) and D(t) for each t in L_a, in both orientations. The old cover members and their covers remain. Each D(t) is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](b); D(1)=U_a, so these added opens cover the added member. All new maps are restrictions of the identity of U_a. This is a permitted presentation by [def-nagata-finite-affine-gluing-presentation], including its original identity and cocycle maps. Only finitely many opens were added, since both the main chart set and all L_a are finite. In particular every t in L_a is now a labelled basic-open element, even when its basic open is empty.

proof.text: Apply [def-nagata-affine-gluing-coefficient-stage] to the enlarged selected presentation from step 2, retaining all its original and added marked basic-open elements in the initial seed. This definition asserts a nonempty directed set of finite affine subring models containing every finite seed, and defines a selected index lambda_coeff for this presentation whose tuple contains its initial seed. Let K_a be the MAIN-CHART component of that selected tuple at lambda_coeff, rather than the component of an unrelated model. Thus K_a is a finitely generated integer subring of A_a and contains every added label t in L_a, as well as every original label. Apply the CURRENT statement of [lemma-nagata-affine-gluing-coefficients-descend] at this very selected stage. For every retained original piece p:a to b it supplies the small map rho_{p,0}:K_b -> (K_a)_{f_p} and the explicit equation j_{a,f_p} composed with rho_{p,0} = rho_p composed with j_b, where j_b is inclusion and j_{a,f_p} is the localized inclusion checked in step 1. For each z in K_b this equation identifies rho_p(z) with the image of rho_{p,0}(z). Hence rho_p(K_b) is contained in (K_a)_{f_p} inside (A_a)_{f_p}, exactly the stability condition for every ORIGINAL piece. The descent statement applies to the selected tuple of this enlarged marked record; it supplies no additional hypothesis on the original arbitrary raw tuple B. Since E_a is contained in K_a, the whole subring B_a=Z[E_a] is contained in K_a. Hence C_a is contained in K_a, and K belongs to the ORIGINAL I(C) by [def-nagata-affine-raw-refinement-system]. Set B'=K. Then B<=B' and T_a is contained in B'_a for every a. The selected index here belongs to the enlarged presentation; it is not identified with the coefficient index of the original presentation. Only its tuple of actual subrings and restricted maps is used to form B' in the original preorder.

source.place: Order 335, entire statement, applied to the presentation enlarged in step 2; supporting source Stacks 07RN (lemma-approximate), finite affine induction

proof.text: Fix a main chart a. The set I(C) is a subset of the finite product of the power sets of the A_b, and its thin category is therefore small. For any x in A_a apply step 3 with B=C, T_a={x}, and the other T_b empty. Thus the union of the subrings B_a is A_a. To check the colimit in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] directly, take any compatible family of unital ring maps mu_B:B_a -> R. Define u(x)=mu_B(x) at any B with x in B_a. If B and B' both contain x, step 1 gives H above both and compatibility gives mu_B(x)=mu_H(x)=mu_B'(x), so u is well-defined. For x,y choose one H containing representatives of both, again using step 1. The identities for u(x+y), u(xy), u(-x), u(0), and u(1) follow from the corresponding identities for mu_H. Thus u is a unital ring map. It restricts to every mu_B and is unique because every x occurs at some B. This is exactly the required universal property of the inclusion cocone.

source.place: Tag 07RN (lemma-approximate), conclusion that the directed coefficient-ring colimit is the original ring; universal property checked explicitly

proof.text: All comparisons remain the inclusions of [def-nagata-affine-raw-refinement-system]. For a fixed original piece p:a to b and f=f_p, the localized family has union (A_a)_f: given x/f^n, step 3 provides a B containing x, while f belongs to every B_a. Equality of x/f^n and y/f^m in (A_a)_f means f^k(x f^m-y f^n)=0 in A_a for some k; after choosing one B containing x and y, the same equality holds in B_a. Thus the displayed fraction equality already holds in (B_a)_f by [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. For a compatible cocone nu_B:(B_a)_f -> R, define v(x/f^n)=nu_B(x/f^n) at any B containing x. If y/f^m is another representative at B' and the two fractions are equal in (A_a)_f, choose H above B and B' by step 1. The annihilating-power equality just proved holds in H_a, so nu_H(x/f^n)=nu_H(y/f^m); cocone compatibility identifies these with the chosen values. Thus v is independent of both the fraction representation and the stage. To verify addition and multiplication choose one H containing x and y: their fraction formulas have numerators x f^m+y f^n and xy and denominators f^(n+m), all in (H_a)_f, so applying nu_H gives the addition and multiplication identities for v. The fractions -x/f^n, 0/1 and 1/1 give preservation of negatives, zero and one. Hence v is a unital ring map, restricts to each nu_B, and is unique because every fraction is represented at a stage. This verifies the localized colimit universal property in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For z in A_b choose B containing z. The map on that representative is rho_{p,B}(z), whose image is rho_p(z) by its defining restriction. If B<=B', both routes in the piece-map comparison send z to exactly rho_p(z), and the localized transition sends x/f^n to x/f^n. Therefore the induced limiting map is the ORIGINAL rho_p on every z, with all comparisons the prescribed actual maps. This uses no open-preservation, inverse or cocycle equation at a finite tuple.
